false_claims.why: _allocateFunds has one call site, processOrder (src/ReelPayoutDesk.sol line 155). Line 147 reverts ValueExceedsOrderCeiling for any amount above 75,000e18 and line 148 reverts ValueExceedsIssuanceLimit, using checked arithmetic on the pre-addition values, when the running total would pass issuanceLimit (never above ALLOCATION_HARD_LIMIT = 40,000,000e18, lines 83 and 118). The total therefore never exceeds 4e25 and cannot wrap; these are the two guard lines the draft itself quotes.

The PoC deploys ReelPayoutDeskHarness, a subclass that adds an external exposeAllocateFunds() forwarding to the internal function, and calls only that; it never calls processOrder(). The function does not exist in src/ReelPayoutDesk.sol, so nothing was observed on the contract as written and the programme's PoC rule (in-scope source as written, external and public functions) is not met.

No listed impact is demonstrated. Through the real entry point an account without an authority signature is credited nothing (InvalidAuthority, line 152), withdraw() reverts InsufficientFunds, and even an authority-signed order for the draft's amount reverts at the ceiling. No inflated balance can exist on the contract as written: withdraw() has nothing to convert into tokens and the reserve cannot be drained this way, so the Critical row does not apply and nothing in the draft is reportable (info at most).
